english: people damn what they do not understand

terms.comment: Adapted from Quintilian 10.1.26, who warns readers of great authors nē, quod plērīsque accidit, damnent quae nōn intellegunt, “not to condemn, as most people do, what they do not understand”. The sentence as Traupman gives it we have not found in an ancient author.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, cited by printed page; each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
